title: tool-calling-exec-ergonomics: multi-tool parallel calls, result injection and robust retries
author: Ethan Kim
files_changed_summary: redwood/runtime/tool_calling.py, redwood/runtime/kv_cache.py, redwood/api/openai_compat.py, redwood/sdk/python/redwood/tooling.py, redwood/console/eval/fixtures/tool_calls.json, tests/test_tool_calling_parallel.py, tests/test_tool_injection_retries.py, docs/api/tool-calling.md, examples/multi_tool_workflow/README.md
description: Motivation: Improve execution ergonomics for tool/function calling when multiple tools are invoked in-parallel or in sequence, ensure deterministic result injection, and provide robust retry semantics that are compatible with OpenAI-style tool calling. Design summary: 1) Add a MultiToolExecution coordinator that tracks in-flight tool calls, supports parallel invocation with configurable concurrency limits, and performs deterministic result injection into the LLM response stream. 2) Add a lightweight idempotency+retry layer for tool calls that distinguishes transient failures (retryable) from terminal failures and surfaces structured retry metadata to the API layer. 3) Extend OpenAI compatibility layer to accept tool result injections as structured events during streaming (preserves existing streaming contract and adds a compat shim for clients that expect tools to emit functions and content). 4) Update KV cache interactions so injected tool outputs are considered for prefix caching and do not invalidate KV state unexpectedly. Backwards compatibility: Default behavior preserves current single-tool semantics; new behavior is gated behind a top-level flag in the tool call request and by a rollout feature flag. Tests: unit tests for coordination and idempotency, integration tests executing multi-tool example workflows, end-to-end streaming test with openai_compat enabled. Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout to 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor latency and error rate dashboards, then 50% for 72h, then full rollout. Migration notes: SDKs receive a helper that serializes tool results into the new structured event format; older SDKs continue to work because we keep the legacy single-tool code path. Implementation notes: split into smaller commits to ease review and revert if needed; included thorough tests and doc updates.

Default behavior unchanged unless feature flag enabled.
